title: Christie's auction of Johnny Marr's guitar collection triples estimate to reach $4.7 million
summary: A dream opportunity that has captured the hearts and imaginations of fans, collectors and music aficionados around the globe, the gavel has gone down on the final lot in Christie's auction Marr's Guitars: The Johnny Marr Collection. The 111 lot sale realised a total of £3,649,280 – more than tripling the estimate. A fitting tribute to the most influential guitarist of his generation, the auction welcomed registrants from 34 countries, with 81% new to Christie's, who bid passionately throughout, from the lowest priced lots offered through to the iconic guitars, resulting in the sale lasting over 5 hours. Opening in style, following a video screened with Johnny Marr and Noel Gallagher riffing on their favourites, fierce competition was evident from the outset with lot 1 selling for more than seven times the estimate. This was swiftly followed by Johnny Marr's 1982 Rickenbacker 330 Jetglo - for many fans, the guitar most strongly associated with Johnny Marr's melodic Smiths-era sound

title: The Merchant House presents André de Jong and His Theater in Amsterdam
summary: With André de Jong and His Theater, The Merchant House presents new works by the distinguished Dutch artist André de Jong (b. 1947). His fifth major exhibition at TMH, it reflects one of the most prolific periods of his career—which has encompassed drawing as well as photography, sculpture, and land art—and poses the question: What is it about drawing, above all, that has continued to fascinate André de Jong for over five decades? We see unquestionable value in de Jong’s works, which seem to defy the limits of the line’s graphic force. For de Jong, the value is in his method: “I enact a performance, grab a sketchbook…” Taking the theatrical to heart, the installation for André de Jong and His Theater fills the walls of the gallery with unframed, overflowing paper panels from his new body-landscape series and other drawings. title: Milestone's Oct. 17 Premier Antique & Vintage Toy auction offers collectors rarities
summary: As their auction catalog testifies, page after page, Milestone’s toy team reached for the top shelf in selecting the lineup of superstars for their October 17 Premier Antique & Vintage Toy Auction. Milestone’s co-owner Miles King traveled from coast to coast several times this year, visiting quietly-held private collections that he described as “very low profile, but very high quality.” He returned with some of the finest consignments his Ohio-based company has handled since they first opened for business 12 years ago. “I think collectors are going to be thrilled when they see what’s in this sale,” King said. “There are prototypes, toys never before seen at auction, and some toys so rare that only one or two others are known to exist. title: Christie's New York presents Graphic Alchemist: Works from the Estate of Frank Stella
summary: Christie's Prints and Multiples Department announced a sale dedicated to the printing practice of twentieth century icon, Frank Stella, consigned by the artist's estate. The sale comprises 65 lots ranging in scale, technique, and formal composition, and acts as a survey of his most inventive and innovative works in the medium. Estimates range from $3,000 to $80,000. The online auction is open from September 24 - October 22, with highlights on view at Christie's Rockefeller Center from September 25 – 30 and October 16 – 20. Unlike many of his contemporaries, Stella's relationship with printmaking became inseparable from his identity as an artist. title: A Parisian apartment reimagined as a living environment for art, conversation and discovery
summary: From 19-24 October, during Art Basel Paris, Sotheby's and _POLIMENO will present Chez Sotheby's, a living environment that brings together art, dining and cultural exchange within an extraordinary Parisian apartment. Neither an exhibition nor a restaurant in the conventional sense, it will showcase exceptional works of Modern, Post-War and Contemporary Art in a setting designed for gathering, discovery and dialogue. Located on Rue de Rivoli, overlooking the Jardin des Tuileries and steps from both Art Basel Paris and Sotheby's Paris, Chez Sotheby's reimagines a long European tradition in which collecting is as much about gathering as it is about acquiring. For one week only, it will become part of the rhythm of Paris: a destination between openings and appointments where connections are forged and discoveries happen naturally. title: Sotheby's presents psychological art exhibition ahead of Hong Kong auctions
summary: On view through 27 September, PSYCHO: Identity Alienation Shadow Duality examines the tensions, desires and contradictions that lie beneath the surface of modern life. Drawing on the psychological language of cinema and literature, the exhibition explores how obsession, vanity, fear and ambition can fuel artistic innovation while revealing the darker realities concealed behind outward appearances. Bringing together an exceptional group of works from around the world, PSYCHO features museum-quality loans from important private collections alongside major highlights from Sotheby's Modern & Contemporary Art Evening and Day Auctions on 28 - 29 September. title: Nivaagaards Malerisamling brings overlooked women artists into its 19th-century galleries
summary: Nivaagaards Malerisamling is expanding the story told by its 19th-century galleries with the addition of two works by women artists whose careers unfolded at a time when access to professional artistic life was still sharply limited by gender. Beginning September 19, 2026, the museum will present newly acquired paintings by Bolette Puggaard and Elisabeth Jerichau Baumann in a focused display within its permanent collection. The works, Italian Landscape by Puggaard and Portrait of Margrethe Lehmann, painted around 1853 by Jerichau Baumann, have recently undergone conservation and will be shown at the museum for the first time. Their arrival marks an important step for a collection that has been working to strengthen the representation of women artists in its historic holdings. title: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods to curate Sotheby's Contemporary Curated auction
summary: Six-time NBA All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns and entrepreneur, model Jordyn Woods will curate the latest edition of Sotheby's Contemporary Curated auction, bringing their shared perspective as collectors and cultural tastemakers to the biannual sale. Together, they represent a new generation of culturally engaged collectors, while Towns joins a growing roster of elite athletes turning a competitive eye for excellence toward the art world. Drawing on their passion for contemporary art, Towns and Woods have assembled a highly personal selection of 10 works by leading postwar and contemporary artists, including George Condo, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein, Helen Frankenthaler, Alma Thomas, John Chamberlain and Rashid Johnson. Spanning painting, sculpture, and works on paper, the sale reflects a dynamic cross-section of artistic innovation across generations. title: Arne Glimcher curates Asher Liftin exhibition at 125 Newbury in Tribeca
summary: 125 Newbury presents Asher Liftin: Recent Work, an exhibition of new paintings and drawings by the Brooklyn-based artist on view from September 18 through October 31 at 395 Broadway in Tribeca. Following Liftin’s Summer 2026 Artist Residency at The Watermill Center in Watermill, New York, the exhibition is curated by Arne Glimcher and accompanied by a written introduction by Glimcher in the gallery’s 125 Free Press publication. Asher Liftin’s work investigates fundamental conditions of vision and visibility. Using his own photography as source material, he translates mechanical images refracted in a glass eye into meticulously hand-crafted renderings on canvas and paper. The resulting images both evoke and extend histories of pointillism and divisionism, summoning the tradition of painters from Paul Signac to Chuck Close. title: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art hosts Europe's first major Remedios Varo retrospective
summary: The Spanish-Mexican painter Remedios Varo (1908-1963) is the subject of a major retrospective opening at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Denmark on 18 September, marking the first presentation of her work on this scale in Europe. In recent years, Varo has attracted renewed attention as one of Surrealism’s most original figures and a pioneering feminist artist. The exhibition features the artist’s most significant works on loan from museums in Mexico and the US alongside key works from private collections that are rarely exhibited publicly. With her singular blend of precision and poetry, Remedios Varo conjures a Surrealist world of mysterious musicians, eccentric scientists, strange contraptions and enigmatic travellers inhabiting imaginary landscapes and uncanny interiors. title: Belgian artist Ann Veronica Janssens debuts new site-specific works in Tokyo
summary: The Fondation d’entreprise Hermès is presenting 5 Chome 4-1 Ginza, Tokyo, the first solo exhibition in Japan of Ann Veronica Janssens (b. 1956, Folkestone, UK). She is a Brussels-based Belgian artist who is active in the international art scene. Since the late 1970s, Janssens has consistently pursued experimental endeavours, employing simple materials like plywood, glass, and concrete, and since around 1990s, also incorporating elements such as light, sound, and artificial haze. Her work spans a wide range of media, including sculpture, installation, video, photography, and stage design for contemporary dance performances. While sharing common interests with artistic movements such as Minimalism, which uses industrial materials and questions the inherent nature of the exhibition space, as well as Light and Space, which offers a scientific examination of perceptual phenomena such as light, volume, and scale, Janssens’ work manifests in the form of subtle, understated intervent

title: Sadie Coles HQ presents recent works by American artist Catherine Murphy
summary: This September, Sadie Coles HQ, Bury Street, presents recent works by Catherine Murphy (b. 1946, Cambridge, MA), marking the artist’s second solo exhibition in London. Since the 1970s, Murphy has transformed the quotidian into the extraordinary, with painted views of existing and imagined scenarios staged in and around the artist’s home and studio in Poughkeepsie, New York. Although Murphy’s meticulous commitment to realism once situated her within the tradition of still life, over the past two decades her practice has shifted from direct observation towards more psychologically charged and subtly surreal interpretations of the objects that populate her surroundings. Focusing on overlooked and unexpected viewpoints, Murphy reframes and resizes the familiar. Idiosyncratic glimpses of objects are reproduced to unsettling effect, their character transformed through a careful choreographing of scenes and use of partial, cropped compositions, and heightened colour. title: Maçka Art Gallery opens 50th anniversary season with Alkan Avcıoğlu's The Death of the Camera
summary: In its 50th anniversary year, Maçka Art Gallery opens its new season with The Death of the Camera, Alkan Avcıoğlu’s first solo exhibition in Turkey, on view from September 15 through October 31, 2026. Presented in collaboration with DIFOART, the exhibition brings together 20 large-scale prints that reconsider photography at a moment when the photographic image is no longer bound to the camera. The exhibition takes its title from Roland Barthes’s 1967 essay The Death of the Author, which displaced the author as the final authority over the meaning of a text. The Death of the Camera carries this idea into the photographic image, addressing the camera’s diminishing authority over how that image is constructed. The single viewpoint, continuous space, and stable relations of scale historically associated with the camera cease to operate as fixed conditions. title: Ben Brown Fine Arts presents Surface Tension exhibition celebrating 1990s British painters
summary: Ben Brown Fine Arts presents Surface Tension, an exhibition of paintings by British artists Peter Doig, Hurvin Anderson, Chris Ofili, Gary Hume, Cecily Brown and Glenn Brown, whose practices were forged in the London art world of the 1990s. Bringing together paintings, drawings and prints made between 1996 and the present, the exhibition traces the parallel history of that decade, telling the story of the painters who, against the prevailing weather, declared that painting remained a medium adequate to its moment. In ‘90s Britain the art world was dominated by the conceptual hegemony of the YBA movement. Damien Hirst, Tracey Emin, Rachel Whiteread, Sarah Lucas and their peers commanded tabloid headlines and museum surveys alike with their readymades, installations and vitrines. title: NASA Engineer's Rolex 'Paul Newman' Daytona brings $200,000 to lead sale
summary: A magnificent Rolex “Paul Newman” Cosmograph Daytona that belonged to pioneering NASA engineer Oran W. Nicks sold for $200,000 Sept. 16 to lead Heritage’s Watches & Fine Timepieces Signature® Auction to $3,683,964. Fresh to the collector market and offered by Nicks’ son, the Rolex Important & Rare Ref. 6239 “Paul Newman” Cosmograph Daytona, Circa 1969 was the top result in an auction filled with rare luxury watches and collectible timepieces from many of the world’s most celebrated manufacturers. The $200,000 Rolex Ref. 6239 carried impeccable provenance. Nicks (1925-98) was a distinguished aerospace engineer who joined NASA in 1960 and became Director of Lunar and Planetary Programs, overseeing early American missions to the Moon, Mars and Venus, including Ranger, Surveyor, Lunar Orbiter and Mariner. title: Lisson Gallery presents first Los Angeles exhibition of Oliver Lee Jackson
summary: Lisson Gallery presents its first Los Angeles exhibition of painter, sculptor, and printmaker Oliver Lee Jackson. A Bay Area resident based in Oakland, Jackson builds his compositions around the human figure, a recurring presence that underpins his work’s structure. This presentation brings together works spanning several decades of his practice from paintings to a group of marble and mixed media sculptures. His sculptural output, a lesser-known but vital aspect of his oeuvre, was last seen in a monumental commission of metal figures for New York’s High Line in 2024, while these forms are being presented publicly for the first time. After initially carving marble in Carrara, Italy in the 1980s, Jackson took to sculpting sensuous figures from stone and wood, but often left the unfinished works aside as he ruminated over their final forms. title: Klodin Erb and Monika Emmanuelle Kazi exhibit at Centre culturel suisse, Paris
summary: Exploring the emotions, fantasies, and big questions that life throws at us, Klodin Erb presents her first personal exhibition in France. Sustained by art history, theatre, fashion, or popular culture, her work interrogates our desires, our concerns, and our ways of inhabiting the world. Le Grand Drame (The Great Drama) floods the space like a scene in which tragedy rubs shoulders with the burlesque and sensitivity blends with the absurd. Her figures evolve in a universe that is at once theatrical, sensual, and profoundly alive. The colorist and gestural painting, imbued with surrealist moments and humanity, simultaneously becomes décor, stage set, and character. Beneath the skylight, venusinfurs deploys a series of monumental paintings within frames made of fabric. title: Salt Beyoğlu presents major survey of Turkish artist and educator Özer Kabaş
summary: Across the Seas: Özer Kabaş and His Times examines the practice of artist, educator, and writer Özer Kabaş (1934–1998), ranging from painting and design to film and theater. It highlights Kabaş’s interest in various artistic disciplines, his approach to art education, and his contributions to Turkey’s cultural landscape. Kabaş studied painting at the Yale School of Art from 1957 to 1962. He learned from structured methods of Josef Albers, a principal figure in shaping the Bauhaus curriculum at Yale, and the expressive style of painter Jack Tworkov, who had joined the faculty as a visiting professor in 1961. Kabaş was also influenced by New Images of Man, curated by Peter Selz at MoMA in 1959, which presented an alternative to Cold War Abstract Expressionism. title: Eric N. Mack challenges conventions of painting in new gallery exhibition
summary: Eric N. Mack radically reconsiders the conventions of painting using textiles as his primary materials. For his second exhibition with Paula Cooper Gallery, Mack presents new free-standing and wall-based paintings, along with a site-responsive installation. This exhibition, titled after a text by the artist quoted in full below, follows recent one-person exhibitions at the American Academy of Arts and Letters, New York, and the Wexner Center for the Arts, Columbus, Ohio, as well as residencies at the Speed Art Museum, Louisville, Kentucky, and BOFFO, Fire Island, New York. Both invoking and disrupting the flat pictorial plane, Mack’s abstract compositions occupy space in ways that challenge traditional understandings of painting. title: Samdani Art Foundation partners with Kunsthalle Basel for the Samdani Art Award 2026 and Regionale 27
summary: Samdani Art Foundation announced a new partnership with Kunsthalle Basel to co-organize the Samdani Art Award 2026 within Regionale 27, supported by the Swiss Arts Council Pro Helvetia. Eight Samdani Art Award finalists from Bangladesh will exhibit alongside sixteen artists from the Regionale at Kunsthalle Basel, opening November 28, 2026, bringing together artists from Bangladesh and the wider Basel region without geographical division. The exhibition, entitled Far Reach, is curated by Diana Campbell, Founding Artistic Director of Samdani Art Foundation, and Mohamed Almusibli, Director and Chief Curator of Kunsthalle Basel, with Yana Kadykova, Curatorial Assistant, Kunsthalle Basel; Ruxmini Reckvana Q Choudhury, Curator, Samdani Art Foundation; and Swilin Haque, Curatorial Assistant, Samdani Art Foundation. title: States of Uncertain Domesticities brings questions of home, identity and belonging to Rome
summary: What does it mean to feel at home at a time shaped by migration, environmental crisis, social change and growing precarity? That question lies at the center of States of Uncertain Domesticities, an international traveling exhibition opening September 19 at the Museo Carlo Bilotti – Aranciera di Villa Borghese in Rome. On view through November 8, 2026, the exhibition examines the idea of home not simply as a physical structure, but as a place shaped by memory, relationships, care, identity and political realities. After previous editions in Berlin at Haus Kunst Mitte and in Brno at the House of Arts, the project arrives in Rome with new works and perspectives developed in response to the city’s cultural and historical setting. title: Tell Me Where Home Is exhibition opens at Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg
summary: What does “home” (German: Heimat, pl.: Heimaten) mean today? Is it even a geographical place, or rather a feeling, a memory, an illusion? How do people in the twenty-first century continually create new homes? In its thematic exhibition Tell Me Where Home Is, the Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg explores the currently intensely debated questions regarding home, migration, and belonging. For even our globalized and digitized societies are imbued with a longing for home—despite, or perhaps precisely because, constant change and migratory movements have become the norm. War, persecution, and the climate crisis are forcing millions of people to leave their homes. Only a small fraction enjoys mobility as a cosmopolitan way of life. title: Melbourne Winter Masterpieces CARTIER: NGV exhibition dazzles 200,000 visitors in Melbourne
summary: The National Gallery of Victoria’s blockbuster exhibition, CARTIER, which closes on 4 October, has dazzled more than 200,000 visitors since it opened in Melbourne in June. Created by London’s Victoria & Albert Museum in partnership with the NGV, and in collaboration with Maison Cartier, the exhibition features nearly 400 extraordinary jewels, timepieces and precious objects owned and worn by the likes of Elizabeth Taylor, Grace Kelly, Rihanna, Andy Warhol, Princess Margaret, The Duchess of Windsor, Dame Nellie Melba, the Maharaja of Patiala, the Begum Aga Khan III, and heiresses including Daisy Fellowes and Barbara Hutton. Exclusive to Melbourne, this adapted and expanded presentation of CARTIER features nearly 300 works never-before-seen in Australia.
